claims.statement: Tom Allen died in 1903.
For the past three months before his death, Tom Allen was in poor health.
Tom Allen has been confined to his bed for two or three weeks with persistent colds and is believed to be seriously ill.
Tom Allen has pains in the arms, ribs and stomach where his opponents' punches landed in past battles.
Don Murphy, manager of Allen's place, said Allen would soon be out again, but that his illness had told on him considerably.
Tom Allen has been confined to his bed for two or three weeks with persistent colds and is believed to be seriously ill.
Don Murphy, manager of Allen's place, said Allen would soon be out again, but that his illness had told on him considerably.
Tom Allen is now ill at his home on Market street.
Allen took to his bed about six weeks before his death, around late February 1903, and was given the best of attention.
Tom Allen planned to marry his nurse, Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove of St. Louis, as soon as he recovered from his illness; the paper gives her age as 21 (headline).
When Mrs. Taylor tried to see her father at the Baptist Hospital after the report of his engagement, she was told he was too ill to talk to anyone.
Tom Allen died in St. Louis about one month before this article was printed.
Tom Allen was taken to the hospital on Friday, 27 March 1903, a week before the article.
Tom Allen's housekeeper, Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove, said the two were to be married when Allen recovered from his illness, which began at Christmas.
On Saturday, March 28, 1903, the attending physician diagnosed Allen's illness as pneumonia and advised his removal to a hospital.
On Saturday, March 28, 1903, Allen was removed to the Baptist Hospital at Garrison and Franklin avenues.
Allen's daughter, Mrs. Mary Taylor, went to the Baptist Hospital with Robert Lyons on Monday, March 30, 1903, and was refused admittance a second time.
Mrs. Taylor said her mother and sister were living in Birmingham, England.
Tom Allen is seriously ill.
Tom Allen had died, and his body lay at an undertaking establishment.
Tom Allen, retired champion pugilist of the world, died at the Baptist Hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis, on the morning of 5 April 1903.
Tom Allen died on Sunday, April 5, 1903, at the Baptist Hospital in St. Louis, at the age of 6- (printed; the last digit is cut off).
Tom Allen, retired champion pugilist, died early on the morning of April 5, 1903, at the Baptist Hospital.
Tom Allen died in St. Louis on April 5, 1903, from general debility.
Tom Allen died at the Baptist Hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis, at 7:35 a.m. on Sunday, April 5, 1903.
Tom Allen died on 6 April 1903, still operating Sportsmen's Rest.
Allen's funeral was expected on Wednesday morning, April 8, 1903, from his home over No. 615 Market Street.
At Allen's funeral on Wednesday, April 8, 1903, from Wand's undertaking establishment, his daughter Mrs. Polly Taylor and Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove stood on opposite sides of the bier.
Tom Allen's funeral took place at 2 p.m. on April 8, 1903, from the Farley & Wand undertaking establishment at 211 South Sixth Street.
Former prize fighters, including Chris Lauff, J Fletcher, Tom Kelly, Andy Kirk, Tom O'Donnell and Gus Ellis, were pallbearers at Allen's funeral.
Allen's daughter Polly Taylor stood by the coffin at the funeral with her four children.
Tom Allen was buried in St. Louis on Wednesday, April 8, 1903.
Charlie Daly, Chris Lauff, Jack Fletcher, Tom Kelly, T. Neusel, Tom O'Donnell and Gus Ellis were pallbearers at Allen's funeral and agreed to serve on the benefit committee.
Tom Allen's funeral procession went to the cemetery on Wednesday, April 8, 1903.
Tom Allen announced he would marry Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove, 21, a trained nurse, on April 23, 1903, his 65th birthday.
